newsitem.title: FRANCE: Egyptian purchase lifts wheat prices at Dunkirk.
newsitem.headline: Egyptian purchase lifts wheat prices at Dunkirk.

text.p: Egypt's purchase of half a million tonnes of French wheat underpinned wheat prices on Tuesday at Dunkirk, a northern port favoured for exports to Egypt because of its large cargo handling capacity, dealers said.
Dunkirk wheat for February was bid at 855 francs and offered at 860 francs per tonne, up five francs on Monday. Rouen wheat for February was steady at 855-860 francs per tonne.
Dunkirk wheat usually trades at a five franc discount over Rouen wheat. But dealers said Dunkirk was the only French port with the capacity to handle the 50,000-tonne cargoes destined for Egypt.
Egypt over the weekend bought 10 cargoes of 50,000 tonnes of French wheat at prices ranging from $140.50 to $143.90 per tonne fob for shipment in February, March and April.
Last week 52,000 tonnes of French wheat also destined for Egypt were loaded at Dunkirk under a previous contract.
French cash grain prices exclude carrying charges of 3.64 francs per tonne, which must be added for every half-month between August 1 last year and the delivery period in question.
